# Document The Rising ToneForge SFX in SFX_CONVENTION.md (full game audio profile)

## Goal

As an engine maintainer, I want The Rising's ToneForge-generated face-off SFX
documented as a first-class game audio profile in the shared
`docs/SFX_CONVENTION.md`, so sibling game repos have a complete, copyable
reference for the convention (keys, deterministic regeneration, runtime wiring,
fallback behaviour).

## Problem statement

`docs/SFX_CONVENTION.md` documents the `sfx-` key convention, asset
organisation, playback helpers and collision protection, and it carries one
ToneForge precedent section (`## Main Street Synth SFX`). The Rising already
ships three ToneForge-generated face-off sounds, but the shared convention has
no The Rising entry — so the doc is incomplete for sibling repos and the
game-side knowledge lives only in `tce-the-rising/README.md`.

## Existing state

- `docs/SFX_CONVENTION.md` (in this repo) has no The Rising section, and the
  `## Audio Asset Organization` tree lists `default/`, `golf/`, `sushi-go/`,
  `feudalism/`, `beleaguered-castle/`, `lost-cities/`, `main-street/` — no
  `the-rising/`.
- The Rising keeps its audio in its **own** repo
  (`tce-the-rising/public/assets/audio/the-rising/`), loaded through the
  pinned `core` submodule; no assets are vendored into the engine.
- The game README (§ *Regenerating the face-off SFX*) already records the
  authoritative facts:
  - `sfx-face-off-reveal` → `face-off-reveal.wav` —
    `tf generate --recipe card-treasure-reveal --seed 42`
  - `sfx-float-in-whoosh` → `float-in-whoosh.wav` —
    `tf generate --recipe whoosh-air-swish --seed 43`
  - `sfx-land-tick` → `land-tick.wav` —
    `tf generate --recipe card-timer-tick --seed 44`
  - keys in `THERISING_SFX_KEYS` (`src/scenes/TheRisingConstants.ts`), file
    mappings in `THERISING_AUDIO_FILES`, preloaded via `preload()` +
    `audioPathWithFallback`, played only via `SoundManager`/`safePlaySound`.
- The game plays all three beats when reduced motion is enabled (no travel, but
  audio still fires).
- The Rising has **no** ToneForge synth mapping module (unlike Main Street's
  `example-games/main-street/sfx-tf-mapping.ts`) — playback falls through to
  committed WAV assets.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — `docs/SFX_CONVENTION.md` gains a `## The Rising ToneForge SFX` section
  documenting the three keys, their asset filenames under
  `public/assets/audio/the-rising/`, and the exact deterministic
  `tf generate --recipe <recipe> --seed <int> --output <path>` command for each
  (seeds 42 / 43 / 44 as recorded in the game README).
- AC2 — The `## Audio Asset Organization` tree gains a `the-rising/` entry
  noting the assets live in the game repo
  (`tce-the-rising/public/assets/audio/the-rising/`), mirroring the existing
  Main Street parenthetical.
- AC3 — The profile records runtime wiring: keys declared in
  `THERISING_SFX_KEYS` (`src/scenes/TheRisingConstants.ts`), file mappings in
  `THERISING_AUDIO_FILES`, loading through `preload()` +
  `audioPathWithFallback()`, playback only through
  `SoundManager`/`safePlaySound` (`no-direct-sound-play` rule).
- AC4 — The profile records reduced-motion behaviour: with reduced motion
  enabled the face-off animation is instant but all three SFX beats still play.
- AC5 — The profile states fallback behaviour: the three face-off WAVs are
  game-specific with no `default/` equivalent, the nine baseline SFX fall back
  to `default/`, and there is no ToneForge synth mapping for The Rising (so
  playback resolves to WAV assets).
- AC6 — The profile links the game-side reproducibility instructions
  (`tce-the-rising/README.md` § *Regenerating the face-off SFX*) and states the
  section is maintained in the engine because sibling game repos read this doc.
- AC7 — Documentation-only change: no engine code, constants or behaviour is
  altered, and `npm run build` + `npm test` pass on the docs branch.
- AC8 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
  code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- AC9 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- UK English.
- Docs-only: no engine code behaviour change; no new engine SFX keys.
- Do not copy The Rising's WAV assets into the engine repo (assets stay in the
  game repo, referenced by path).
- Only `docs/SFX_CONVENTION.md` is expected to change; `CHANGELOG.md` is managed
  by the release pipeline.
- Landed on engine `dev` through the normal flow. Producer decision
  (2026-10-19): the consuming game repo (`tce-the-rising`) pins its `core`
  submodule to the **`dev` commit containing this change**, rather than waiting
  for the `dev` → `main` release promotion — so the commit SHA must be reported
  on completion for the cross-repo pointer bump.

## Key Files

- `docs/SFX_CONVENTION.md` — new `## The Rising ToneForge SFX` section; add
  `the-rising/` to the `## Audio Asset Organization` tree.

## Related work

- Cross-repo tracker: **RISE-0MVBUSQUR006LPVP** (tce-the-rising) — blocked by
  this item; on completion it bumps its `core` submodule pointer to this item's
  engine `dev` commit and verifies the doc renders in-tree. Report the commit
  SHA in the completion comment so the game-side bump is deterministic.
- `RISE-0MVBKG7VK003JIDH` (tce-the-rising) — generated the three WAVs and
  recorded the recipes/seeds this section documents.
- Precedent: `## Main Street Synth SFX` in the same doc, and
  `example-games/main-street/sfx-tf-mapping.ts` for the synth-mapping contrast.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk (drift):** recipes/seeds recorded in the game README could diverge from
  this section. Mitigation: quote the exact commands and link the README section
  as the authority.
- **Risk (inverted dependency):** documenting another repo's assets in the
  engine could imply the engine owns them. Mitigation: state explicitly that
  assets live in the game repo and the engine only owns the convention text.
- **Assumption:** the three recipe names/seeds in the game README are the
  committed, reproducible values (verified there; recorded in
  RISE-0MVBKG7VK003JIDH as byte-identical on regeneration).
- **Assumption:** a docs-only engine change still needs the normal
  build+test gate, per engine policy.
data.title: Document The Rising ToneForge SFX in SFX_CONVENTION.md (full game audio profile)

# Manually test the story-line extraction (core + Main Street)

**Goal:** As a developer/QA, manually exercise the extracted generic story-line system and confirm the mechanic behaves exactly as before, that the Gym demo works, and that the documentation matches observable behaviour.

## Context

The branching story-line mechanic was extracted from `tce-main-street` into the generic, game-agnostic `@story-line` module in this repo (see work item `CG-0MVH2H67H002M27B`). Main Street now consumes it through thin adapters. This item is the **manual acceptance pass** that complements the automated parity/full-suite gates.

- Core module: `src/story-line/` (alias `@story-line`).
- Gym demo: `example-games/gym/scenes/GymStorylineScene.ts`.
- Core reference: `docs/core-engine/story-line.md`.
- Consumer: `tce-main-street` at `dev` 87486479 (core submodule `fab1ce28`).

## Prerequisites

- Core checkout at the current `dev` `fab1ce28`; sibling `tce-main-street` at `dev` 87486479 with its `core` submodule pinned to `fab1ce28` (already the state in this workspace).
- Launch with `GAMES_CONFIG=full npm run dev` so both the Gym and Main Street load in the Game Selector (plain `npm run dev` shows only the Gym). Record the seed when starting a Main Street run so determinism checks (AC 3) can be reproduced.
- Record the exact steps taken, observed results, build/commit tested, and any screenshots or notes in a comment before closing.

## Acceptance criteria

- **Gym demo walkthrough.** Run `npm install && npm run dev`, open the Gym, select **Storyline**, and verify:
  - the Town Meeting card presents **Invest** / **Ignore** with the default UI adapter's choice-clarity labels;
  - choosing **Invest** applies the Town Meeting card's own effect (Lose 50 coins, −50) and deals **Public Investment**, which offers **Celebrate** / **Double down**;
  - choosing **Celebrate** applies Public Investment's +120 coins and deals the terminal **New Beginning** card; **New Beginning** (no options) applies its +60 reputation effect and ends the chain ("Chain complete");
  - a terminal option (**Double down** / **Let it be**) ends the chain immediately with no successor;
  - **Reset** restarts the demo from Town Meeting; the journal/status panel tracks the choices.
- **Main Street shipped storylines.** In `tce-main-street`, play each of the five shipped arcs (tax, health, economy, labour, restaurant) and verify manually:
  - the dialog title is the storyline name and the subtitle is the incident name;
  - the option labels and choice-clarity labels match the documented semantics (apply vs skip, no escalation card revealed);
  - choosing an option applies the expected coin/reputation effect and deals the documented successor (or ends the chain for terminal options);
  - the **Story update** activity-log line and the Storyline Journal entry match the chosen option;
  - undo/redo of a choice and a save/load round-trip preserve the pending/resolved choice and its option snapshot.
- **Determinism.** With the same game seed, replaying a storyline produces the same presented options and successor selection (one seeded draw per candidate selection).
- **No regression.** Non-storyline incidents still resolve as plain incidents (no choice dialog); terminal escalation cards carrying a `storylineId` (`evt-general-strike`, `evt-farm-table`, `evt-depression`, `evt-pandemic`) do not become choices.
- **Docs match reality.** `docs/core-engine/story-line.md` (core), `docs/game/storylines.md` (Main Street) **and the Gym scene's in-scene help "Test plan" text** accurately describe the adapters, the Gym demo and the manual steps above; report any drift as a follow-up.

## Suggested test data

- Shipped CSV: `tce-main-street/src/card-data.csv` (storyline ids `storyline-tax`, `storyline-health`, `storyline-economy`, `storyline-labor`, `storyline-restaurant`).
- Gym fixture: the in-scene cards in `GymStorylineScene.ts`.

## Out of scope

- Automated test coverage (already green: parity gate + both full suites).
- New storyline authoring / conditional options (tracked separately).

## Notes

- Record the exact steps taken, observed results, build/commit tested, and any screenshots or notes in a comment before closing.
- If a behaviour differs from the pre-extraction behaviour, file a bug and reference this item.
- Known drift to confirm during the pass: the Gym scene's help "Test plan" attributes +120 coins to Invest (it actually arrives on choosing Celebrate); confirm on screen and file the follow-up.

**Goal:** Add cost-gating, extra effects, and declarative conditional successors to the generic story-line option model in core, enabling game authors to express options that are only available when the player can afford them, branch differently based on game state, and carry their own consequences.

## Provenance

Refilled from `tce-main-street` epic **MS-0MUNB58TK0025CB9** after the story-line engine was extracted into this repo's core module (`src/story-line/`). The epic, its plan revision, producer decisions (Q1–Q3), assumptions, and risks are preserved verbatim; only the target paths and scope have been adapted to TCE core.

## What landed before this epic

- The generic story-line engine was extracted to `src/story-line/` with the game-agnostic adapter seam (`@story-line` alias, parity tests, Gym demo): **CG-0MVH2H67H002M27B**.
- CSV `options` encoding supports arbitrary labels and candidate sets (`parseStorylineOptionsEncoding`).
- `PendingStorylineChoice.options` provides a draw-time frozen snapshot of the compiled option list.

## Existing state (verified against `src/story-line/`)

- `StorylineOption` (`src/story-line/types.ts`) carries `label`, `successorId?`, `successorIds?`, `effectPolicy`, `condition?`, `successorResolver?`.
- `CompiledStoryline` wraps an ordered option list.
- `compileStorylineFromEvent()` (`src/story-line/compile.ts`) compiles registry > CSV > legacy, with draw-time `condition` filtering.
- `resolveStorylineOption()` (`src/story-line/resolve.ts`) applies `effectPolicy`, resolves successor with documented precedence (callback > random draw > single id), computes deltas via `adapter.getResources(state)` before/after.
- `createPendingStorylineChoice()` / `getPendingStorylineOptions()` (`src/story-line/index.ts`) manage the pending-choice lifecycle with a draw-time snapshot.
- `StorylineEngineAdapter` (`src/story-line/types.ts`) provides `rng()`, `applyEffect()`, `getResources()`, `appendLog()`, etc. — the **only** path from core into game state.
- None of `cost`, `extraEffect`, or `conditionalSuccessors` exists anywhere in `src/story-line/` — these are genuine remaining gaps.

## Desired change

Extend the in-memory model and resolution path so that:

1. Options declare an optional declarative affordability `cost`; the draw-time presented list additionally filters out unaffordable options.
2. Options declare an optional `extraEffect` and ordered declarative `conditionalSuccessors`, both applied/selected at resolution time.
3. Selection applies `effectPolicy` (unchanged), deducts `cost`, applies `extraEffect` independently, and pushes the resolver-precedence successor.
4. A `validateStorylineOptions()` helper validates cost/extra-effect/condition data; the Gym demo remains a green smoke test.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Backwards-compatible model extension.** `StorylineOption` gains optional `cost`, `extraEffect`, and `conditionalSuccessors` fields; omitting preserves current behaviour.
2. **Cost gating.** Options whose `cost.coins` exceeds `getResources(state).coins`, or whose `cost.reputation` exceeds `getResources(state).reputation`, are omitted from the presented list; no-cost options always included.
3. **Presented list stability.** `PendingStorylineChoice.options` stores the draw-time snapshot populated at choice draw time; the presented list is computed once at draw and is stable.
4. **Cost deduction.** Selecting an affordable option deducts cost coins and cost reputation from `state` via the engine adapter's resource-mutation seam.
5. **Extra effects.** Any `extraEffect` is applied after cost deduction, independently of `effectPolicy`; both can coexist.
6. **Loss checks and logging.** Cost deduction and extra effects are reported in `coinChange`/`repChange` deltas; `appendLog()` captures the operations. Consumer-side loss checks fire when resources drop to zero (unchanged).
7. **Conditional successors.** `conditionalSuccessors` evaluated sequentially; first rule matching `getResources(state)` determines pushed card ID; `successorId` fallback.
8. **Boundary coverage.** All boundary cases tested: above/below threshold, equality boundary, no-match fallback; matched successor via `pushChainCard`.
9. **Precedence.** `successorResolver` callback wins when present; otherwise conditional rules run before `successorIds` random draw and legacy `successorId`; a matching rule consumes no RNG draw.
10. **Cost-aware consumer scoring.** The `getPendingStorylineOptions` snapshot gives consumers (e.g. Main Street AI) the cost-filtered list to score — no core AI in scope.
11. **Determinism.** All new semantics are pure/declarative; no new RNG. Gym demo runs to completion without stalls.
12. **Static validation.** `validateStorylineOptions()` rejects negative/zero costs; unknown field or op; non-numeric value; negative extraEffect; dangling conditional successors.
13. **Shipped content.** Existing CSV-encoded cards, Gym fixtures, and parity tests validate cleanly; the doc-drift / docs-consistency test passes.
14. **Documentation.** `docs/core-engine/story-line.md` documents the extended `StorylineOption` fields, cost filtering, extra effects, conditional successors, and resolution lifecycle with examples.
15. **Seam and authoring docs.** `src/README.md` and `docs/DEVELOPER.md` confirm new semantics are programmatic via `registerStorylineOptions`, not CSV-authored.
16. **Parity regression.** All existing unit/smoke/parity tests remain green with zero behavioural deltas.

## Constraints

- **Programmatic authoring only (producer decision Q1=A).** Extend the in-memory model, engine resolution, and validator. The CSV `options` column does not gain cost/extra-effect/conditional authoring — those stay programmatic via `registerStorylineOptions`.
- **Declarative and serialisable (producer decision Q3=A).** Only field/op/value conditions and numeric deltas.
- **Game-agnostic seam.** New semantics live behind `StorylineEngineAdapter` and keep the module determinism intact.
- **Affordability is coins and/or reputation (producer decision Q2.1).** All specified costs must be affordable.
- **Omit, do not disable (producer decision Q2.2).** Unaffordable options are removed from the presented list.
- **Cost is a real payment (producer decision Q2.3).** Deducted in addition to the option's effectPolicy.
- No shipped card content is expected to use the new semantics; existing gameplay must remain byte-for-byte equivalent.
- **Full suite gate.** Every child's DoD includes a green full project test suite (`npx vitest run --project unit`); the epic is not complete until all parity/regression tests pass with zero behavioural deltas.

## Core adaptation notes

These differences from the original Main Street epic must be resolved during implementation:

- **Resource mutation seam.** `StorylineEngineAdapter` has `getResources(state)` but no `applyResourceDelta(state, { coins, reputation })` method. Cost deduction and extra effects require extending the adapter. **Design option:** add an optional `applyResourceDelta` to the adapter interface (with a default no-op for existing implementors) so core remains compatible. The child items document this as an open design note.
- **Resources at compile time.** `compileStorylineFromEvent(event, registry, state)` currently receives only `state` for condition callbacks; cost filtering needs `getResources(state)`. The `createPendingStorylineChoice()` wrapper (which has the full `StorylineSystem` instance) can supply an optional `getResources` function or extend the signature.
- **No AI in core.** `decideEventChoice` (Main Street AI scoring) is a consumer concern. The core module provides the cost-filtered snapshot via `getPendingStorylineOptions`; Main Street updates its AI to read it. Tracked separately as **MS-0MUNB58TK0025CB9-C7**.
- **No CSV pipeline/validator in core.** `validateStorylineOptions()` validates registered/compiled options programmatically. JSON schema and `storyline-graph.ts` are Main Street concerns.
- **Docs location.** Canonical docs at `docs/core-engine/story-line.md` and `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (not `docs/game/`).

## Risks

- **Adapter API change.** Extending `StorylineEngineAdapter` with `applyResourceDelta` is a breaking change for existing adapter implementors (Main Street, Gym). *Mitigation:* optional method with sensible default, migration note, and parity gate.
- **Cost filtering changes the index space.** The draw-time snapshot (`PendingStorylineChoice.options`) already freezes the presented list, so cost filtering inherits that stability — but consumers must read the snapshot. *Mitigation:* `getPendingStorylineOptions` returns the cost-filtered snapshot; parity/regression tests cover this.
- **Precedence ambiguity.** Two successor mechanisms now coexist (callback resolver, declarative rules) plus random candidate sets. *Mitigation:* precedence documented in code and tests (callback > declarative rules > random candidates > single successor).
- **Scope creep.** Callback conditions/resolvers already ship; CSV label authoring already shipped. This work adds only cost/extraEffect/conditionalSuccessors.

---

## Producer decisions (preserved from original)

- **Q1=A** — Programmatic only; no CSV column authoring.
- **Q2.1** — Gates: coins and/or reputation.
- **Q2.2** — Omitted, not disabled.
- **Q2.3** — Real payment (deducted in addition to effectPolicy).
- **Q3=A** — Declarative, serialisable data.

## Plan summary

| # | Child | Title | Dependency |
|---|-------|-------|------------|
| 1 | C1 | Extend StorylineOption model with cost, extraEffect, conditionalSuccessors | (none) |
| 2 | C2 | Add cost-based affordability filtering at draw time | C1 |
| 3 | C3 | Deduct cost and apply extra effects at resolution | C1, C2 |
| 4 | C4 | Resolve declarative conditional successors | C1, C2, C3 |
| 5 | C5 | Validate declarative option metadata (new helper + tests) | C1, C4 |
| 6 | C6 | Update documentation for extended option model | C3, C4, C5 |

## Related work

- **CG-0MVH2H67H002M27B** — Generic story-line system in core (completed; parent context for this extension).
- **MS-0MUNB58TK0025CB9** — Original epic in Main Street (being deleted after refile).

## Problem statement

Under CPU contention the Vitest **browser** stage can fail with

    Error: Failed to import test file <path>
    Caused by: TypeError: Failed to fetch dynamically imported module: http://localhost:<port>/<path>

while every other file passes and the same files pass on a quiet machine. That is
the Vite dev server failing to serve a module under load — the same class of
transient contention failure as the worker-RPC timeout and the browser WebSocket
drop that `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` already retries — but it is not in the
runner's recognised signature set, so the run is never retried and the gate fails
spuriously.

## Users

- **Producer / release engineer** running `/skill:test` or `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh`
  on a loaded workstation: "When the only thing that broke is the vite dev server
  dropping a module fetch under load, I want one automatic retry instead of
  re-running a 20-minute suite by hand."
- **Agent implementing a work item**: "I need the push gate to be a verdict about
  my code, not about ambient CPU contention."
- **Maintainer of the retry runner**: "I need the new signature to stay inside the
  existing attribution discipline, so a real broken import is never excused."

## Acceptance Criteria

- A browser run whose only errors are the module-fetch signature
  (`Failed to fetch dynamically imported module`) is retried **exactly once**, and
  accepted as green only when the retry is clean (exit 0 / all files passed).
- Acceptance of this signature requires the retry to be green: a run where **both**
  attempts show the module-fetch signature is reported as a failure and never
  `accepted-transient`. A genuine module-resolution regression (mistyped import
  path, deleted file, 404 on an asset module) is deterministic and must surface.
  The existing all-passed-signature acceptance path (CG-0MUF0LU4X006IXXU) is
  unchanged for the two original signatures.
- A run containing any error that is not attributable to a transient signature
  (e.g. an `AssertionError`, or a `Failed to import test file` block without the
  module-fetch cause) is never retried and never accepted as green.
- The signature is a named exported constant
  (`MODULE_FETCH_SIGNATURE`) and is documented in the runner header comment as a
  fourth contention signature alongside the existing three (worker RPC timeout,
  browser WebSocket drop, true hang), with the same "every error block must
  contain it" attribution rule (`failuresAreTransientOnly`).
- Project-coverage semantics are unchanged: acceptance still requires the executed
  file set to match the expectation, and it is verified (unit test or documented
  reasoning) that a failed-to-import file still appears in the captured executed
  set so the coverage gate does not turn the retried-green run into a
  `[coverage-failed]` exit.
- Unit tests in `tests/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.test.ts` cover: positive
  (module-fetch-only failing run retried, clean retry returns the retry's status),
  both-attempts (not accepted, `outcome=retry-failed`/`failed`), and negative
  (module-fetch signature alongside a genuine assertion failure → no retry).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the change, including code
  comments, the runner header, `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh`'s header comment,
  `AGENTS.md` and `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (both enumerate the transient signatures).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- `tests/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.test.ts` is the runner's own regression
  suite; the new fixtures must be additive and must not weaken the existing
  masking-guard pins (including the verbatim CG-0MUIMM28K001W88F incident
  fixture).
- The runner must stay byte-for-byte identical in behaviour when no expectation
  is supplied and no transient signature is present (no change to exit codes for
  genuine failures).
- No product/runtime code changes — this is test-tooling robustness only.
- Fix must not require Vitest/Vite configuration changes (the failure is a
  loaded-machine artefact, not a misconfiguration).
- Matching is Chrome/Chromium-specific text (`Failed to fetch dynamically imported
  module:`); Firefox emits a different message. Scope the constant to the Chromium
  text that the browser project actually uses, and note the limitation in a
  comment rather than inventing an untested pattern.

## Existing state

- `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` recognises exactly two transient signatures
  (`WORKER_TIMEOUT_SIGNATURE`, `BROWSER_DROP_SIGNATURE`) via
  `hasTransientSignature` / `failuresAreTransientOnly`, plus the third
  (non-retryable) hang signature detected by the wall-clock bound.
- `shouldRetryOnce` retries when the summary is all-passed plus a transient
  signature, or when failures exist but every error block is attributable to a
  transient signature; if the retry is also purely transient the run is accepted
  (CG-0MUF0LU4X006IXXU).
- The opt-in project-coverage gate (`--expect-project-coverage`, on for the unit
  and browser stages) makes a file-set mismatch a genuine failure.
- Incident evidence (CG-0MVHZ2RBJ004O0VD, commit `f9762665`, load avg ~8):
  `tests/core-engine/tf-runtime-integration.browser.test.ts` failed to import and
  `tests/handView/gym-handpile-outlines.browser.test.ts` had 4 tests fail to fetch
  `example-games/gym/createGymHandPileGame.ts`; `attempts=1 outcome=failed`; the
  same commit's browser stage passed 37/37 files on a quiet machine.

## Desired change

1. Add `MODULE_FETCH_SIGNATURE` (`Failed to fetch dynamically imported module`) as
   an exported constant beside the two existing signatures, with the incident
   shape documented in the header comment as signature 4.
2. Extend the attribution predicates so this signature makes a run retryable under
   the same every-error-block rule.
3. Keep acceptance of a both-attempts-poisoned run limited to the pre-existing
   signatures: the new signature is **retry-only** recovery, so the retry's own
   exit status stands.
4. Add positive / both-attempts / negative fixtures and tests to the runner suite.
5. Update the signature enumerations in the runner header,
   `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh`, `AGENTS.md` and `docs/DEVELOPER.md`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` — add `MODULE_FETCH_SIGNATURE`, extend
  `hasTransientSignature` / `failuresAreTransientOnly`, restrict the
  both-attempts acceptance path, update the header comment.
- `tests/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.test.ts` — new fixtures
  (module-fetch-only failing run, both-attempts variant, genuine-assertion
  counter-case) and the corresponding `shouldRetryOnce` / `runWithRetry` tests.
- `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` — header comment enumerating the transient signatures.
- `AGENTS.md` — testing section ("retries once on Vitest's transient
  contention-induced failures …") must list the new signature.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — `#### CPU-contention mitigation (unit and browser tests)`
  section (signature list, `shouldRetryOnce` shape list, acceptance rule).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Masking risk (primary).** A genuine broken import emits the identical text.
  Mitigation: retry-only recovery plus the every-error-block attribution rule; the
  both-attempts acceptance path is deliberately *not* extended.
- **Coverage-gate interaction.** If a failed-to-import file were absent from the
  JSON reporter's executed set, the coverage gate would reject the run regardless
  of the new signature; the incident summary (`Test Files 1 failed`) suggests it is
  counted, but implementation must confirm the executed-set capture still matches.
- **Pattern brittleness.** Chromium's message may change or Firefox may be used;
  pin the exact Chromium substring and keep the unit fixtures as the contract.
- **Scope-creep guard.** Broader HTTP-level retries (dev-server 5xx, asset 404s),
  `webServer` timeout tuning, and generic "any import failure is transient" logic
  are out of scope; file them as separate work items if they prove needed.
- **Assumption:** the incident is contention-triggered, not a code defect — the
  same commit's browser stage passed 37/37 files on a quiet machine.

## Related work

Manual context (the automated find-related report is appended below):

- CG-0MVHZ2RBJ004O0VD — the run that surfaced the gap (story-line management UI).
- CG-0MUIMM28K001W88F — attributable failed-file transient (retry discipline).
- CG-0MUF0LU4X006IXXU — accept when both attempts are pure transient.
- CG-0MT08R2QR0070F3N — wall-clock hang bound (never retried).
- CG-0MVL21CVM003VK5H — project-coverage gate.
- CG-0MS9M5UJP005PWD3, CG-0MSCI73RH004VPCE — the original two signatures.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **No interview round was required.** The item's goal, incident evidence and
  acceptance criteria already resolved the two decisions that would otherwise
  have been asked:
  1. *Does the new signature get the both-attempts acceptance path?* — Answered by
     AC "accepted when the retry is green" plus Scope's "a genuine
     module-resolution regression is never masked": **no**, retry-only recovery.
     Recorded as an explicit AC bullet so the decision is auditable.
  2. *Chromium-only, or a cross-browser pattern?* — Answered by repo search: the
     browser project runs headless Chromium only
     (`scripts/check-browser-test-env.ts`), so the Chromium text is the contract.
- Duplicate check performed — no overlapping item found (`wl search` on
  "dynamic import transient retry" and "Failed to fetch dynamically imported
  module"; only this item and unrelated completed work matched).
## Implementation notes (plan review)

Planning is auto-completed for this item: the description already carries
measurable acceptance criteria, a five-step desired-change sketch and a
validated `**Key Files**` list (all five paths exist), so no child
decomposition is needed — the change is one coherent edit across the runner,
its regression suite and three documentation surfaces (effort Small, risk
Medium). Details below are intent-preserving notes for the implementer; none
of them changes an acceptance criterion.

1. **Acceptance predicate split.** `runWithRetry` currently reuses
   `shouldRetryOnce(second.result.output)` for the both-attempts
   `accepted-transient` path. Retry-only recovery therefore needs a *separate*
   acceptance predicate (restricted to `WORKER_TIMEOUT_SIGNATURE` and
   `BROWSER_DROP_SIGNATURE`), while `hasTransientSignature` /
   `failuresAreTransientOnly` gain `MODULE_FETCH_SIGNATURE`. A module-fetch
   failure on both attempts must then fall through to `outcome=retry-failed`
   carrying the retry's exit status.
2. **Retry-banner wording.** The `[retry]` message hard-codes
   "(worker RPC timeout or browser connection drop)"; extend it (and the
   `[transient-accepted]` / header text as applicable) so the diagnostic does
   not contradict the recognised signature set.
3. **Verify the real error-block shape.** `errorBlocks()` starts a block at
   each `…Error:` line and `failuresAreTransientOnly()` requires *every* block
   to contain a signature. The incident shape is
   `Error: Failed to import test file <path>` followed by
   `Caused by: TypeError: Failed to fetch dynamically imported module: …`. If
   Vitest prints the cause on its own line starting with `TypeError:`, the
   header block would carry no signature and the run would never be retried.
   Pin the verbatim shape in the fixture and, if the cause is a separate block,
   document the attribution treatment chosen in the runner header and cover it
   with a test.
4. **Coverage-gate evidence.** The acceptance criterion requires showing that a
   failed-to-import file still appears in the captured executed set; record that
   evidence (test or documented reasoning) alongside the runner's coverage-gate
   comment.

## OPEN QUESTION: exact Vitest error-block shape for the module-fetch incident

Directed to: whoever holds the CI log for CG-0MVHZ2RBJ004O0VD (commit
`f9762665`). Why it matters: attribution only retries when *every* error block
contains the signature, so if `Caused by: TypeError: …` is emitted as a block
of its own the header block is unattributable and the new signature would never
trigger a retry. Resolution is evidence-gathering only (capture the verbatim
output as a fixture); the acceptance criteria are unchanged.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MT00JNOP003KVH8** – Split non-tutorial browser test suite into per-instance chunks to fix CI context-exhaustion regression (completed)
- **CG-0MT08R2QR0070F3N** – Browser test stage hangs on gym overlay tests during full-suite npm test under CPU contention (completed)
- **CG-0MUIMM28K001W88F** – [test-failure] <suite exited 1>: npm --silent test — failing test (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: 0ms9m5ujp005pwd3, 0msci73rh004vpce, 0mt08r2qr0070f3n, 0muf0lu4x006ixxu, 0muimm28k001w88f (+320 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: 0mt08r2qr0070f3n, 0muf0lu4x006ixxu, 0muimm28k001w88f, 0mvl21cvm003vk5h, absent (+266 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: 0ms9m5ujp005pwd3, 0msci73rh004vpce, accept, actually, add (+190 more)

# Core illegal-move routine: explain a rejected move with a reason toast

**Headline:** The shared illegal-move feedback routine in `core/src/ui/` must
render the player-facing rejection reason as a transient toast, so every game
that reuses the helper explains refusals instead of only shaking the card.

## Goal

As an engine maintainer, I want the core illegal-move routine to accept a
reason string and display it as a transient toast — independently of the shake
branch — so every game built on the core explains rejected moves consistently
without writing its own overlay.

## Problem statement

`shakeIllegalMove` (`core/src/ui/shakeIllegalMove.ts`) today plays
`sfx-illegal-move`, tints and shakes the target, and drops everything else. The
rules layer already produces a player-facing sentence for every illegality
(`LegalityResult.reason`), and the game's in-game help promises that a rejected
move is "rejected with the reason" — a promise no engine or game code currently
keeps. The shake and the sound are also the only feedback for players with
reduced motion or audio off, which is an accessibility gap.

The engine half is tracked by this item; the game-side wiring and the submodule
pointer bump are tracked by **RISE-0MVPAAWIV003CE3D** in the
`tce-the-rising` store.

## Users

- **The player** — needs to know *why* a move was refused ("which card blocks
  it, or which figure I could never have met") so they can pick a legal slot.
- **The player with reduced motion / no audio** — today only gets a shake and a
  sound; the toast is the explanation channel.
- **Game developers using the core engine** — want consistent illegal-move
  feedback (shake, sound, explanation) from one entry point.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — The core routine renders the reason.** The shared illegal-move feedback helper in `core/src/ui/` accepts an optional `reason` and, when present, renders a transient toast containing that exact text. With no reason the current behaviour (tint + shake + `sfx-illegal-move`) is unchanged for existing consumers — the parameter is optional and adding it does not alter other games.
- **AC2 — Toast behaviour.** It is non-blocking (never swallows pointer input intended for cards, slots or buttons), appears above the board/overlays at a depth taken from `core/src/ui/constants.ts`, auto-dismisses after a configurable dwell (~2.5 s default), can be dismissed early, and is ephemeral (not persisted, not part of undo/redo or the transcript).
- **AC3 — Shown on every feedback branch, reduced motion included.** The toast is rendered by the core routine independently of the shake branch, so it appears when the target is a tintable `Image`/`Sprite`, when it is a non-tintable `Container`, and when reduced motion (`core/src/ui/ReducedMotion.ts` / `prefers-reduced-motion`) suppresses the shake entirely. Under reduced motion the toast still appears unobscured and is readable for its full dwell with no slide/fade animation; the existing shake-suppression behaviour is unaffected.
- **AC4 — Repeat rejects replace, never stack.** A second rejection inside the dwell window replaces the current text (and restarts the timer) instead of stacking duplicates; the toast is destroyed on scene shutdown so it cannot leak across scenes.

# Engine: game-specific events, catch-all and forwarding

## Goal

As the maintainer of any game built on the Tableau Card Engine, I want the engine to let my game declare its own typed event names and payloads, and to forward every emitted event — core or game-specific — to the Phaser bridge and the debug event buffer without per-game name lists, so a new logging tool subscribes to a stable vocabulary instead of re-deriving game state, while the engine itself stays game-agnostic.

Cross-repo companion to The Rising item RISE-0MVO0075N005E9WZ (child RISE-0MVPYD4GX008LAFR). No The Rising vocabulary lives in the engine; the engine only ships the mechanism.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Games can register game-specific, typed events.** `core/src/core-engine/GameEventEmitter.ts` gains a documented, **additive** mechanism for a game to declare its own typed event names and payloads via a game-extensible `GameEventMap`: a game augments the exported `GameEventMap` interface (`declare module '<specifier>' { interface GameEventMap { 'my-event': MyPayload } }`). `on`, `once`, `off` and `emit` continue to work over the merged map, and **no** game-specific name is added to the engine. The chosen mechanism (interface augmentation, as opposed to a generic `GameEventEmitter<M extends GameEventMap>` parameter) and its rationale are recorded in the module doc comment. **Ships with an engine-level unit test**: a game declares a map, emits through it, and receives on `on` and `onAny`.
- **AC2 — Catch-all subscription.** `GameEventEmitter` gains `onAny(listener: (eventName, payload) => void): () => void`, which fires for **every** emission regardless of name (engine or game-specific), with the same snapshot semantics as `on` (a listener may unsubscribe during an emission without skipping peers), returning an unsubscribe function. `emit` stays a no-op when no listeners are attached.
- **AC3 — Phaser bridge forwards every event.** `PhaserEventBridge` receives **every emitted event — core or game-specific — without maintaining per-game name lists (catch-all subscription)**, so a game-specific event reaches `scene.events` with no per-game name list. The existing Phaser → engine direction (a hard-coded wiring of *known* names) is kept, documented as such (an un-typed Phaser side cannot be enumerated), and its behaviour is unchanged.
- **AC4 — Global event buffer forwards every event.** `GlobalEventBuffer.subscribe` receives **every emitted event — core or game-specific — without maintaining per-game name lists (catch-all subscription)**, so game-specific events are buffered from session start and the dev "Game Events" overlay receives them automatically.
- **AC5 — Testing / validation.** Engine unit tests cover the extension mechanism and catch-all forwarding using a **synthetic game event**: a dedicated test fixture module augments `GameEventMap` with a synthetic game event; tests assert that (a) the augmented name is emittable and receivable via `on`, (b) `onAny` receives both the synthetic and the engine names with the right payloads, (c) unsubscribing stops delivery, (d) unsubscribing from inside an `onAny` handler does not break the iteration, and (e) a synthetic game event emitted on the engine arrives on a `PhaserLikeEventEmitter` through the bridge and lands in `GlobalEventBuffer` entries. Existing core-name tests stay unchanged and green.
- **AC6 — Documentation.** `docs/DEVELOPER.md` gains a "Game-specific events" section with a worked example (augment the map, emit, subscribe per name, subscribe with the catch-all, observe it cross the bridge and reach the buffer) and states the engine-agnostic rule: the engine provides the mechanism, never game vocabulary.
- **AC7 — Additive only.** No core event name, payload shape, export or consumer is renamed or removed; the `gym` example game and every other consumer keep working with no edit required (verified, not assumed).
- **AC8 — No manual changelog edit.** `CHANGELOG.md` is release-pipeline managed and must not be edited by hand; module comments and `docs/DEVELOPER.md` carry the documentation.
- **AC9 — Engine gates pass.** The engine's `npm run build` and changed-scope test gate pass; no ad-hoc full-suite runs during implementation.
- **AC10 — Full engine test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Minimal implementation

- `GameEventEmitter`: add an any-listener collection plus `onAny`, invoked for every emission (even when no per-name listeners are attached), typed `(eventName: GameEventName, payload: GameEventMap[GameEventName]) => void`; snapshot semantics identical to `on`; document the augmentation mechanism in the module doc comment.
- `PhaserEventBridge`: replace the engine→Phaser `ALL_EVENTS` loop with one `onAny` subscription that re-emits `(event, payload)` on the Phaser side; keep the reverse direction and the re-entry guard unchanged.
- `GlobalEventBuffer`: replace the name-list loop with one `onAny` subscription; buffered `events` gain both engine and game names.
- Test fixture `tests/core-engine/fixtures/augmentedGameEventMap.ts` + tests in `tests/core-engine/GameEventEmitter.gameEvents.test.ts` (map + catch-all) and bridge/buffer forwarding tests using the same fixture (synthetic game event).
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — new "Game-specific events" section with the augmentation example.

**Key Files:**
- `src/core-engine/GameEventEmitter.ts`
- `src/core-engine/PhaserEventBridge.ts`
- `src/ui/debug/GlobalEventBuffer.ts`
- `tests/core-engine/GameEventEmitter.test.ts` (existing — unchanged)
- `tests/core-engine/GameEventEmitter.gameEvents.test.ts` (new)
- `tests/core-engine/fixtures/augmentedGameEventMap.ts` (new)
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md`

## Constraints

- **Cross-repo.** Implementing repo: `Tableau-Card-Engine`. The pointer bump in The Rising (`tce-the-rising`) is a separate item (`RISE-0MVPYD68F009Z42E`); blocking relationship is textual — `wl dep` cannot span worklog stores.
- **Additive only, engine-agnostic.** No The Rising names, no rules knowledge, no breaking type change; `gym` and all consumers compile unchanged.
- **No new dependency.** Zero-dependency emitter stays zero-dependency and Phaser-free.
- **Emission is side-effect free.** Emitting with no listeners attached is a no-op.

Non-blocking; small task.
